No, a court would generally not enforce the bar to invalidate the assignment of the $30,000 payment right. A general ban on assigning "the contract" is read as barring only delegation of performance and as a promise not to assign (UCC §2-210; Restatement (Second) of Contracts §322), and UCC §9-406(d) makes anti-assignment terms ineffective against assignments of payment rights (accounts). The distributor could still face breach damages under the clause, and the treatment center can keep paying the distributor until it gets notice of the assignment. I'm not adopting either option in the team note, because both treat the bar as enforceable against the payment right, which conflicts with these rules.

CONFIDENCE: 70
